evidence.quote: Were the FOMC to delay the start of policy normalization for too long, we would likely end up having to tighten policy relatively abruptly to keep the economy from significantly overshooting both of our goals.
economic conditions may, for some time, warrant keeping the target federal funds rate below levels the Committee views as normal in the longer run.
On balance, economic and financial information received since our October meeting has been consistent with our expectations of continued improvement in the labor market.
these downside risks from abroad have lessened since late summer.
core inflation--which ran at 1-1/4 percent over the 12 months ending in October--is also well below our 2 percent objective

When the Committee begins to normalize the stance of policy, doing so will be a testament, also, to how far our economy has come in recovering from the effects of the financial crisis and the Great Recession.

parsed.rationale: The speech signals that liftoff is imminent: data are consistent with expectations, downside foreign risks have eased, and it warns against delaying normalization, while also stressing gradualism and a low neutral rate. Inflation is described as below target but expected to return to 2 percent, so the net signal leans moderately hawkish.
